content: Gentianales is an order of flowering plants that belongs to the asterid group within the dicotyledons. In the Cronquist system, the classification of Gentianales included a broadly defined Loganiaceae (which has since been divided into several families), Retziaceae, Gentianaceae, Saccifoliaceae, Apocynaceae, and Asclepiadaceae. The Angiosperm Phylogeny Group (APG) has redefined the circumscription of Gentianales to include the following families: Apocynaceae (which now incorporates Asclepiadaceae), Gelsemiaceae (separated from Loganiaceae), Gentianaceae (which now includes Saccifoliaceae), Loganiaceae, and Rubiaceae. Under the APG classification, some notable members of Gentianales include coffee plants, gardenias, and frangipani. Additionally, the APG has placed Retziaceae within Stilbaceae, which is part of the order Lamiales.
